name: A loose edge hides a tighter chain
note: C0 allows t2-t0 <= 12. C1 then C2 imply <= 7. The path proves the upper bound; a complete schedule attains it.

name: Each pair is fine. The cycle is not.
note: Three individually satisfiable constraints sum to 0 <= -1. Pairwise opposite-edge checks miss the three-edge global conflict.

name: Disconnected means free, not impossible
note: Two components can translate relative to one another. Every missing directed path gets an anchored ray that grows its time difference without breaking any constraint.

name: Duplicate constraints: remove one at a time
note: Both duplicate edges are individually redundant. Deleting both at once would remove the bound. Redundancy is not a simultaneous deletion plan.

name: A zero cycle is allowed
note: Zero-weight cycles can force equality. Path ties use lexicographic original edge-index sequences among simple paths, not shortest hop count.

name: A conflict outside the anchor component
note: t0 is isolated. The negative cycle on t1,t2 still makes the whole network impossible. Checking only nodes reachable from t0 is insufficient.

name: A negative self-loop
note: The single constraint t0-t0 <= -1 is impossible. A nonnegative self-loop, by contrast, is redundant by the empty path.

name: Only the anchor
note: One time point, no constraints. Its only queried difference is zero; fixing t0=0 just removes a shared translation.

name: Six free time points
note: All off-diagonal upper bounds are unbounded, with explicit translation rays. Every diagonal is exactly zero.

name: Twelve edges, negative values, no negative cycle
note: A six-node directed ring and its reverse bound all relative times. Negative edge weights are allowed; only negative total cycles are inconsistent.

name: The implied bound can exceed every input weight
note: Five weights of 20 imply t5-t0 ≤ 100. The reverse direction is unbounded. Input bounds do not cap inferred bounds or witness times.
